first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence that shortening onboarding improves time-to-value is directly relevant. I would verify that record alongside targeted-pricing evidence because competitor pricing creates a consequential alternative for qualified revenue. A standard experiment should measure completion and activation together with qualified pipeline, conversion, retention, and downstream revenue to ensure gains are sustainable rather than low-quality signups.

final.rationale: Run a guarded simplification of onboarding this week because onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the verified record shows shortened onboarding improved completion, reduced time-to-value, and increased 30-day retention. Measure completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified conversion, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue against a control. Do not use targeted promotional pricing as the experiment: although it increased signup and short-term qualified revenue, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with the sustainable-revenue objective.
